external_entities.name: customer company
external_entities.description: A customer organization using the invoicing service as a tenant.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant

external_entities.name: customer user
external_entities.description: A person at a customer company who uses the billing app as an admin or viewer.
external_entities.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
external_entities.notes: Each user belongs to one company and is either an admin or a viewer.

external_entities.name: payer
external_entities.description: The recipient of an invoice email who can open the payment page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: A support employee who uses the admin console and can open a billing-app session as a customer user.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.

processes.name: billing app
processes.description: The shared invoicing application used by customer users, which serves pages, queries the tenant database, queues PDF jobs, and fetches PDFs.
processes.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform.

processes.name: PDF renderer
processes.description: A worker that consumes render jobs, reads invoices, and writes rendered PDFs.
processes.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time

processes.name: admin console
processes.description: A console reachable from the support office network through which support agents can open sessions in the billing app as customer users.
processes.source_excerpt: The admin console is reachable only from there

data_stores.name: tenant database
data_stores.description: A shared PostgreSQL database containing every company's invoices, customers, and payout bank details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database, the tenant database.
data_stores.notes: Every table has a company ID column. The billing app applies the company filter; the database has no row-level security. The app uses one database account for all companies.

data_stores.name: render queue
data_stores.description: A queue holding PDF render jobs containing a company ID and an invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: To make a PDF, the billing app puts a render job on the render queue.

data_stores.name: PDF bucket
data_stores.description: A shared bucket where the PDF renderer stores PDFs under a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time, reads the invoice from the tenant database and writes the PDF to the PDF bucket
data_stores.notes: The billing app fetches PDFs with one service credential for all companies.

data_flows.name: use billing app
data_flows.description: A customer user uses the billing app in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.authentication: email address and password; session cookie

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A customer user signs in to the billing app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They sign in with an email address and a password and get a session cookie.
data_flows.notes: There is no second factor for admins or viewers.
data_flows.authentication: email address and password; session cookie; no second factor
data_flows.data_description: email address, password, and session cookie

data_flows.name: open invoice
data_flows.description: A customer user opens an invoice in the billing app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a user opens an invoice, the billing app loads it by its invoice number.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the billing app checks that the invoice belongs to the user's company.

data_flows.name: edit invoice
data_flows.description: A customer user submits the whole invoice to the billing app for saving.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The invoice edit form posts the whole invoice back, and the billing app saves every field it receives
data_flows.notes: This includes the paid flag and the company's payout bank account.
data_flows.data_description: whole invoice, paid flag, and company's payout bank account

data_flows.name: ask for PDF
data_flows.description: A customer user requests a PDF of an invoice.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Any user can ask for a PDF of any invoice, as often as they like.

data_flows.name: send invoice email
data_flows.description: The billing app sends an invoice email containing a link to the payer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: invoice link containing the invoice number

data_flows.name: open payment page
data_flows.description: A payer opens the payment page from the invoice link.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details, and it asks the payer to sign in to nothing.
data_flows.notes: The payer is not required to sign in.
data_flows.data_description: invoice, company name, and bank details

data_flows.name: enqueue render job
data_flows.description: The billing app puts a render job on the render queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: To make a PDF, the billing app puts a render job on the render queue.
data_flows.notes: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number.

data_flows.name: read render job
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer takes render jobs from the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time

data_flows.name: read invoice
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer reads an invoice from the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: reads the invoice from the tenant database

data_flows.name: write PDF
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer writes a PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number.
data_flows.notes: The renderer trusts the company ID carried by the job.
data_flows.data_description: PDF, company ID, and invoice number

data_flows.name: fetch PDF
data_flows.description: The billing app fetches PDFs from the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.
data_flows.notes: One service credential is used for all companies.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A support agent signs in to the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code.

data_flows.name: open user session
data_flows.description: A support agent opens a billing-app session as a customer user through the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
data_flows.notes: Everything the agent then does is recorded in the tenant database against that customer user, and not against the agent.
data_flows.authentication: admin-console account and one-time code; customer-user session

trust_boundaries.name: cloud platform
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud platform containing the shared billing app, tenant database, render queue, PDF renderer, and PDF bucket.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform.

trust_boundaries.name: customer company
trust_boundaries.description: The tenant boundary associated with a customer company and its users.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant

trust_boundaries.name: support office network
trust_boundaries.description: The network from which support agents work and where the admin console is reachable.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network. The admin console is reachable only from there

assumptions.assumption: The customer company is represented as an external system because it is an organization outside the invoicing service's control and the model has no organization-specific entity kind.
assumptions.basis: The text describes each customer company as a tenant of the service.

assumptions.assumption: The billing app presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: People use the billing app in their browser.

assumptions.assumption: The PDF renderer is a non-web process.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a worker that takes jobs from a queue and renders PDFs.

assumptions.assumption: The admin console presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is an interactive console used by agents to sign in and open sessions.

assumptions.assumption: The tenant database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It stores invoices, customer information, and payout bank details.

assumptions.assumption: The PDF bucket contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It stores PDFs rendered from invoices, including company and bank details.
